project.researchNotes: Sequential place 14 of 22. Kinneuchar Inn is pub/restaurant-led and removed from Eat. Private loch-shore and estate access is not promoted. Elie and Colinsburgh services are not transferred.

touristAppeal.label: Notable Stop
touristAppeal.summary: Kilconquhar remains a genuine 60–70 visit for its church and old-kirk ensemble, historic village fabric, loch viewpoint and Barnyards Marsh, supported by a local circuit but not by café depth or public toilets.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: Good for a controlled outdoor circuit and unusually strong dog-friendly dining, but wildlife-sensitive marsh and loch viewing, traffic on Main Street and an unconfirmed church-interior policy keep it below the general visitor score.

visitorHighlights.name: Kilconquhar Parish Church, Old Kirk and Loch Viewpoint
visitorHighlights.reason: The village’s most coherent visit combines 12th-century documentary origins, medieval remains, the 1821 church, kirkyard monuments and the confirmed public loch viewing stance.
visitorHighlights.tagline: Old kirk and lawful loch view
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Kirkyard, ruins and viewing stance in daylight; general church-interior hours are not published.
visitorHighlights.admission: Free exterior, kirkyard and viewpoint visit.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Fife Council and Scottish Ornithologists’ Club

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A visibly layered church-and-kirkyard ensemble with an unusual birdwatching viewpoint, reduced for unconfirmed interior access and the private loch shore.

visitorHighlights.name: Kilconquhar Historic Village Trail
visitorHighlights.reason: A genuine community-authored 12-stop circuit gives purpose and interpretation to one of Fife’s densest small listed streetscapes.
visitorHighlights.tagline: Twelve stories through a listed village
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Public streets and paths; visit in daylight.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Colinsburgh Community Trust and Fife Council

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A coherent and interpreted historic-village walk, reduced for digital-only presentation, residential character and limited practical facilities.

visitorHighlights.name: Barnyards Marsh Nature Reserve
visitorHighlights.reason: The short public wetland path adds genuine nature value and links Kilconquhar with Barnyards without claiming access around the private loch.
visitorHighlights.tagline: Small public wetland and village link
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open-air path in daylight; conditions are not staffed or guaranteed.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Fife Council and Colinsburgh Community Trust

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A locally valuable public nature stop with habitat interest and a through-route, reduced for small scale, variable path condition and limited interpretation.

features.fullDescription: Churchyard predominantly to N and E of Kilconquhar Parish Church (see separate listing). Various 18th century monuments and headstones of note. The Scottish Ornithologists’ Club describes public access through the churchyard to a viewing stance; the estate hide is members-only and the loch shore is not a public circuit.

attractionGuide.headline: Church, medieval ruins and the village’s one public loch view
attractionGuide.intro: Read the surviving church phases and kirkyard first, then use the churchyard route to the published birdwatching stance without straying onto private estate ground.
attractionGuide.parking: Fife Council’s Main Street car park is free and has 20 surface spaces. No payment is required; accessible bays, maximum stay and overnight rules are not published on the facility page.
attractionGuide.toilets: Fife Council lists no public toilet in Kilconquhar. Use the official facilities in Elie before or after this stop.
attractionGuide.picnic: The Quiet Garden beside the church is for reflection rather than a promoted picnic site; a simple bench is mapped south of the village.
attractionGuide.foodNote: The Kinneuchar Inn is a highly regarded in-village restaurant and pub; book ahead and confirm current service times.

trails.name: Kilconquhar Village Heritage and Marsh Circuit
trails.summary: A self-guided circuit joining the church, Main Street, Barnyards and the public marsh paths.
trails.difficulty: Mostly village streets and paths; the marsh can be wet, narrow or overgrown.

thingsToDo.name: Separate the church phases
thingsToDo.summary: Compare the present 1821 building with the surviving late-medieval aisle and older grave monuments.

thingsToDo.name: Use the lawful loch viewpoint
thingsToDo.summary: Follow the published route through the churchyard to the viewing stance; do not imply general shore access.

thingsToDo.name: Look for wintering waterbirds
thingsToDo.summary: The shallow SSSI loch is particularly noted for ducks, grebes, coot and moorhen.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A visibly layered church-and-kirkyard ensemble with an unusual birdwatching viewpoint, reduced for unconfirmed interior access and the private loch shore.
